answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 22 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the nadir solution is checked at the pulse gate and logged, the vertex audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. The fee repeats 12 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
